summaries.summary: The page explains the mechanism of action of a drug that disrupts cell membranes, involving membrane disruption, pore formation at the nanometer scale, and membrane depolarization. It outlines a three-step general model: (i) attraction of the agent (AP) to the membrane, (ii) attachment of the AP to the membrane, and (iii) insertion of the AP into the membrane, causing disruption and leakage of ions and metabolites.
key_facts: Mechanism involves membrane disruption and pore formation at the nanometer scale.
Three-step model: (i) AP-membrane attraction, (ii) attachment, (iii) insertion causing disruption and leakage of ions/metabolites.
visible_text: Based on membrane disruption followed by pore formation on the nanometer scale and membrane depolarization.
The following general model for the mechanism of action has been proposed:
(ii) attachment of the AP onto the membrane and
(iii) insertion of the AP into the membrane causing its disruption, leading to the leakage of ions and metabolites.
